title: The Golden Age of Illustration
description: The great illustrators of the storybook and magazine age — Pyle, Wyeth, Parrish, Remington, Gibson, and Shippen Green — in their pre-1931 heyday.

items.title: The Fair Nihilist
items.description_narrative: A woman in an elaborate lace-trimmed gown sits in profile, showing a ring to a mustached man in evening dress while an older man looks on from the shadows behind them. Wikimedia Commons attributes this illustration to Howard Pyle, reproduced in a 1913 issue of Harper's Magazine.
items.tags: magazine illustration, howard pyle, harper's magazine, golden age illustration, interior scene, jewelry, romance

items.title: The Fair Nihilist (companion plate)
items.description_narrative: A cloaked man steps down from a horse-drawn carriage on a rain-slicked city street at night, while a driver in a tall hat holds the reins of the horse in the foreground. Wikimedia Commons attributes this illustration to Howard Pyle, reproduced in a 1913 issue of Harper's Magazine.
items.tags: magazine illustration, howard pyle, harper's magazine, golden age illustration, night scene, carriage, street scene

items.title: They Took Their Wives with Them on Their Cruises
items.description_narrative: A man in a peaked cap studies the horizon through a brass telescope while a woman in a wide straw hat sews beside him and a grinning sailor grips the ship's wheel, sails and open sea behind them. This oil-on-board scene dates to about 1938.
items.tags: sailing, telescope, ship's wheel, seascape, oil on board, nautical

items.title: Arizona Nights
items.description_narrative: Cowboys crowd a shadowy saloon bar as one man leans in close, jaw set and finger jabbing, while others look on tensely with hands near their gun belts. N. C. Wyeth painted this magazine illustration in 1906.
items.tags: n.c. wyeth, cowboys, saloon, american west, tension, illustration

items.title: Arizona Nights (companion plate)
items.description_narrative: Under a hillside mining town, a cowboy levels his revolver at a cluster of onlookers gathered by a corral fence, a coiled lasso lying at his feet. N. C. Wyeth painted this companion scene the same year, 1906.
items.tags: n.c. wyeth, cowboys, standoff, corral, american west, mining town, illustration

items.title: Where the Mail Goes, Cream-of-Wheat Goes
items.description_narrative: A rider in a wide-brimmed hat reaches up to post a letter in a rough wooden mailbox out on the open range, his horse pausing beneath a pale moon in the cold morning air. This advertising painting dates to August 1908.
items.tags: cowboy, mailbox, open range, advertising art, oil on canvas, morning light

items.title: Advertisement for a Smoking Substitute
items.description_narrative: A knight in golden armor stands triumphant with sword drawn, one foot planted on a fallen, helmeted figure, his round shield raised against a hillside and clouded sky. The lettering names the fallen figure Nicotine and the knight's shield No-To-Bac, promising the product kills the tobacco habit. Maxfield Parrish illustrated this advertisement.
items.tags: advertisement, knight, allegory, tobacco cure, maxfield parrish, lithograph, satire

items.title: Harper's Weekly, Bicycling Number
items.description_narrative: Two facing pages show similar images of a rider in a checked jacket on a bicycle, one captioned as a bicycle advertisement and the other as a magazine cover, both set against a leafy green landscape. Maxfield Parrish illustrated the Harper's Weekly Bicycle Number cover shown at right, in 1896.
items.tags: maxfield parrish, bicycle, harper's weekly, cycling, poster art, advertisement

items.title: Scribner's for April
items.description_narrative: A woman in flowing pale robes and a leafy crown leans on a stone balustrade beneath a blossoming tree, framed inside a poster advertising a magazine's April issue, its border crowded with columns of small print listing that month's stories. This lithograph dates to 1899.
items.tags: magazine poster, woman, blossoming tree, lithograph, lettering, art nouveau

items.title: The Christmas Scribner's
items.description_narrative: A bald, portly man in a long red robe strides in profile carrying a round golden object, set beside a column of hand-lettered text listing the issue's contributors. This poster advertises The Christmas Scribner's, a lithograph dated 1897.
items.tags: maxfield parrish, scribner's magazine, poster, art nouveau, christmas, lithograph

items.title: The Century: Midsummer Holiday Number, August
items.medium: Color lithograph (Les Maîtres de l'Affiche, pl. 123)
items.description_narrative: A nude woman sits curled on green grass, knees drawn up and face tipped back toward a canopy of stylized trees dappled with light. Bold lettering above her spells out THE CENTURY, with Midsummer Holiday Number and August set below in a poster announcing the magazine's summer issue.
items.tags: poster, lithograph, magazine cover, maxfield parrish, golden age of illustration, figure
items.credit_line: Les Maîtres de l'Affiche vol 3 sur Gallica

items.title: Harper's Weekly for Christmas
items.description_narrative: A beaming cook in a tall chef's hat, a faint halo-like ring behind his head, holds out a platter bearing a large roasted dish, an ornate lattice window and distant village rooftops sketched behind him. Maxfield Parrish drew this magazine cover in 1895.
items.tags: maxfield parrish, christmas, cook, magazine cover, pen and ink, holiday feast

items.title: Dancer with Cymbals
items.description_narrative: Walter Crane created this illustration in 1895. A dancer with flowing hair and swirling drapery leans backward while striking two cymbals, framed against a dense pattern of leaves and grapevines.
items.tags: walter crane, illustration, art nouveau, dance, line drawing, golden age of illustration, cymbals, ornamental pattern
items.credit_line: Petit Palais, Musée des Beaux-Arts de la Ville de Paris
items.current_repository: Petit Palais, Musée des Beaux-Arts de la Ville de Paris

items.title: Reaper Death
items.description_narrative: A winged, aged figure with vast dark wings swings a scythe low through a meadow of wildflowers where tiny human figures scatter and flee, all bathed in a hazy golden light. Walter Crane painted this allegorical scene in 1900.
items.tags: allegory, death figure, wings, scythe, wildflowers, tempera painting

items.title: A Dream (Voyage de Rêve)
items.description_narrative: A winged, haloed youth rows a small boat across calm moonlit water, a heraldic banner streaming from its mast, while a sleeping woman in white lies among roses and lilies at his feet. Walter Crane made this pastel, titled A Dream (Voyage de Reve), in 1902.
items.tags: walter crane, dream, boat, angel, symbolism, pastel, sleeping figure

items.title: Day of Labour
items.description_narrative: A barefoot allegorical woman in a soft peaked cap stands with arms raised amid garlands of flowers, banners scrolling around her carrying printed lettering. This print reproduces a design attributed to Walter Crane, made sometime between about 1895 and 1920.
items.tags: walter crane, allegory, labour, socialism, phrygian cap, garland, print

items.title: His Word of Honor
items.description_narrative: A robed woman sits turned away on a rock amid a bombed, smoking landscape as a helmeted soldier kneels before her, clutching his chest and pleading, while a grieving, veiled figure kneels among a field of grave markers in the background. Charles Dana Gibson drew this pen-and-ink cartoon in 1917.
items.tags: charles dana gibson, wwi, allegory, satire, pen and ink, war graves, editorial cartoon

items.title: Scribner's for June
items.description_narrative: A young woman in a puff-sleeved blouse and long skirt rides a bicycle straight toward the viewer, rendered entirely in loose, energetic pen strokes with tall block lettering flanking her on either side. This poster dates to 1895.
items.tags: bicycle, pen and ink, poster, fashion, lettering, monochrome

items.title: The Weaker Sex II
items.description_narrative: Four elaborately coiffed women lean over a table, one holding a magnifying glass to a tiny figure of a man no bigger than a pin, their expressions caught between curiosity and amusement. Charles Dana Gibson drew this scene in July 1903.
items.tags: pen and ink, satire, magnifying glass, women, humor, illustration

items.title: The Reason Dinner Was Late
items.description_narrative: A young woman sketches a caricature on an easel pad while three onlookers lean in and a heavyset, mustached man sits waiting at a table set for dessert, the whole scene built from quick, energetic pen strokes. Charles Dana Gibson drew this around 1912.
items.tags: caricature, pen and ink, dinner table, onlookers, humor, illustration
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID cai.2a12863.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Life Was Made for Love and Cheer
items.description_narrative: Guests in high-collared, old-fashioned dress gather beneath a flowering tree and a weeping willow while children play with a dog on stone steps leading to a white house. Elizabeth Shippen Green painted this garden gathering in September 1904.
items.tags: garden party, willow tree, children, dog, old-fashioned dress, illustration
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsc.04735.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: The Navarrese (Plate I)
items.description_narrative: A woman in a flower-trimmed cap and pale rose-patterned gown sits with a blue cloak draped over her shoulders, a red-and-gold tapestry glowing behind her. Elizabeth Shippen Green painted this portrait study in 1907.
items.tags: medieval dress, tapestry, portrait, seated figure, illustration, blue cloak

items.title: The Navarrese (Plate II)
items.description_narrative: In a walled garden at dusk, a man in a red doublet leans close to a woman in a flowing teal gown who cradles a pale shawl, a stone fountain glinting below them. Elizabeth Shippen Green painted this twilight scene in 1907.
items.tags: garden, courtship, twilight, fountain, medieval dress, illustration

items.title: The Navarrese (Plate III)
items.description_narrative: A woman in a flame-red riding habit raises a falcon skyward astride a rearing white horse, leading a mounted hunting party across open grassland. Elizabeth Shippen Green painted this hawking scene in 1907.
items.tags: falconry, horseback, hunting party, medieval costume, grassland, illustration

items.title: The Navarrese (Plate IV)
items.description_narrative: An older woman in a black gown patterned with gold medallions sweeps past a bearded man in a blue robe standing near a stone stairway, a small tapestry hanging on the wall behind them. Elizabeth Shippen Green painted this indoor scene in 1907.
items.tags: medieval interior, stairway, tapestry, formal dress, illustration, confrontation

items.title: The Journey
items.description_narrative: A curly-haired child kneels at a train window, chin propped on folded arms, gazing out at billowing clouds that seem to build into towers and domes above a green valley. Elizabeth Shippen Green drew this quiet reverie in 1903.
items.tags: child, train window, clouds, daydream, illustration, landscape

items.title: The Flowers
items.description_narrative: A barefoot toddler sits on sunlit paving beside a gate, reaching down toward a pitcher overflowing with cut flowers. Elizabeth Shippen Green made this charcoal and watercolor illustration for a 1908 Harper's Magazine story.
items.tags: illustration, watercolor, charcoal, children, flowers, golden age of illustration

items.title: King Lear, Act I, Scene I
items.description_narrative: A woman in flowing cream robes is drawn gently aside by a crowned figure while richly dressed onlookers and two shaggy dogs look on in a torchlit hall hung with antlers and trophies. Edwin Austin Abbey based this large 1898 canvas on King Lear.
items.tags: shakespeare, medieval hall, farewell scene, oil painting, royal court, dogs

items.title: Two Gentlemen in Eighteenth-Century Dress
items.description_narrative: Edwin Austin Abbey drew this interior scene in 1885. A man in a wide-brimmed hat sits with legs crossed in a wood-paneled room, a dog curled at his feet, while another man enters through the doorway carrying a pitcher.
items.tags: edwin austin abbey, pen and ink, illustration, genre scene, 18th century dress, interior scene, golden age of illustration, drawing

items.title: The Right of the Road
items.description_narrative: A loaded stagecoach drawn by four straining horses crowds a narrow mountain trail as a lone cyclist pedals hard just ahead, kicking up snow on the same track. Frederic Remington painted this hazardous encounter in 1900.
items.tags: stagecoach, horses, bicycle, mountain trail, snow, oil painting

items.title: Toro, Toro!
items.description_narrative: A rider swings a lasso overhead astride a rearing horse, a kerchief pulled over his face, dust and stampeding cattle blurring into the background of this wood-engraved magazine page. Frederic Remington drew this in 1893.
items.tags: lasso, rearing horse, dust, cattle, wood engraving, monochrome

items.title: A Quarrel Over Cards
items.description_narrative: A card game turns tense as one man half-rises from his chair, jabbing a finger at another across a lamp-lit table crowded with players, while a bystander watches uneasily from the doorway of a stone-walled room. Frederic Remington drew this saloon scene in 1887.
items.tags: card game, confrontation, saloon, lamp light, monochrome, illustration

items.title: An Indian Dance
items.description_narrative: A dancer in a feathered headdress and fringed regalia moves through a circle of seated onlookers among tall pines and tipis, holding a slender staff, shown here in a black-and-white photographic reproduction of the original. Frederic Remington made this scene in 1903.
items.tags: dance, regalia, tipis, forest camp, monochrome, illustration

items.title: Cowboy on a Bucking Bronco
items.description_narrative: A cowboy grips the reins with one hand as his horse bucks violently beneath him, all four hooves off the ground and his hat flying loose into the air. Frederic Remington painted this bronco-riding scene in 1908.
items.tags: frederic remington, cowboy, bucking bronco, american west, action, illustration

items.title: The Prince and Zoza, with the Story-Tellers (Frontispiece, Stories from the Pentamerone)
items.description_narrative: A royal procession in richly colored robes descends a wide stone staircase past a garden wall, led by a cloaked figure with a staff, while an enormous peacock spreads its tail beside them. Warwick Goble painted this frontispiece for the 1911 Stories from the Pentamerone.
items.tags: illustration, watercolor, fairy tale, warwick goble, golden age of illustration, peacock
items.credit_line: Stories from the Pentamerone (1911), plate facing p.7, "The Prince and Zoza, with the Story-Tellers"

items.title: Mission Building
items.description_narrative: Franciscan friars in brown robes move through a bustling adobe mission compound where workers haul baskets, carry water jars on their heads, and hoist timber scaffolding beneath whitewashed arches. Dean Cornwell painted this sweeping mural scene.
items.tags: mission scene, friars, mural, adobe architecture, laborers, oil painting
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID highsm.24473.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: I Want You for the Navy
items.description_narrative: A young woman in a double-breasted navy uniform and cap poses with hands on her hips, wind lifting her hair, beside bold lettering. Howard Chandler Christy illustrated this recruitment poster in 1917.
items.tags: howard chandler christy, wwi poster, navy, recruitment, lithograph, patriotic

items.title: Virginia Harned as Alice of Old Vincennes
items.description_narrative: A woman in a wide-collared blouse and long skirt cinched with a bright red sash stands holding a slender sword, flowers tucked into her upswept hair. Howard Chandler Christy drew this theatrical portrait in 1902.
items.tags: theatrical costume, red sash, portrait, sword, illustration, actress
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsca.45577.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Clear the Way
items.description_narrative: A woman crowned with a laurel wreath and draped in flag-striped fabric points ahead above a warship's deck crowded with bare-chested sailors loading a massive gun barrel. Bold lettering across the top reads Clear the Way, urging support for a Fourth Liberty Loan bond drive; Howard Chandler Christy illustrated this poster in 1918.
items.tags: howard chandler christy, wwi poster, liberty loan, warship, propaganda, patriotic, lithograph
items.credit_line: This file comes from Gallica Digital Library and is available under the digital ID btv1b6909474b

items.title: Americans All!
items.description_narrative: A woman personifying Liberty raises a laurel wreath before an American flag, beside an honor roll of surnames including Du Bois, O'Brien, Pappandrikopolous, Kowalski and Gonzales, under the banner Americans All and the words Victory Liberty Loan below. This is a Victory Liberty Loan poster held by the U.S. National Archives and Records Administration.
items.tags: liberty loan, wwi poster, immigrants, propaganda, lithograph, patriotic, honor roll
items.credit_line: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration

items.title: The New Generation
items.description_narrative: Two men stand talking on a cottage path lined with flowering vines while a young woman in an apron watches from the doorway, every leaf and shingle rendered in dense, fine pen lines. Franklin Booth drew this scene in 1912.
items.tags: pen and ink, cottage, doorway, fine linework, rural scene, illustration

items.title: The New Generation (Plate II)
items.description_narrative: Two men sit on a rocky coastal bluff gazing out at breaking waves beneath towering, wind-carved clouds rendered in dense, engraving-like pen strokes. Franklin Booth drew this seascape in 1912.
items.tags: pen and ink, coastline, clouds, seated figures, fine linework, illustration

items.title: Give Mother the Vote, We Need It
items.description_narrative: A row of round-faced toddlers in yellow bonnets and coats tumbles forward, one waving a small flag, above bold lettering arranged in blocky rows. The poster is titled Give Mother the Vote, We Need It, and argues that food, health, schools and homes are all ruled by men's votes.
items.tags: suffrage, poster, toddlers, cherubic children, lithograph, votes for women, political poster

items.title: Christmas Eve Memories
items.description_narrative: An elderly couple dozes side by side in armchairs while translucent, ghostly children dance and play around them, one hanging a stocking, another twirling in a tutu. Rose O'Neill drew this pen-and-ink Christmas scene in 1902.
items.tags: rose o'neill, christmas, nostalgia, ghostly children, pen and ink, genre scene, memory

items.title: The Sunday-School Picnic
items.description_narrative: Children and adults spread across a shaded lawn for a picnic, baskets and dishes scattered on blankets while one woman shelters under a parasol and toddlers reach for food. Rose O'Neill drew this scene in 1900.
items.tags: picnic, children, parasol, outdoor gathering, chromolithograph, family

items.title: The Bachelor's Last Christmas Eve
items.description_narrative: A winged cherub aims a toy arrow across a cluttered room where one man lounges wearily in an armchair by the fire and another, dressed to go out, looks down with a wary glance; scattered linens and an open bag lie on the floor between them. Rose O'Neill drew this Christmas Eve satire, published as a color lithograph in 1900.
items.tags: rose o'neill, cupid, bachelor life, satire, fireside, color lithograph, christmas eve

items.title: When We All Believe
items.description_narrative: Santa Claus kneels amid a crowd of children reaching toward him and his sack of toys, some laughing, some tumbling over each other in excitement. Rose O'Neill drew this scene in 1903.
items.tags: santa claus, children, christmas, chromolithograph, crowd scene, toys
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsca.25801.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: The Next Candidate for Statehood
items.description_narrative: A girl in a fringed shawl reaches shyly toward a reclining, flag-draped figure who beckons her forward beneath a garment bearing the word 'Statehood.' Rose O'Neill drew this cover image in 1901.
items.tags: statehood, political cartoon, personification, cover illustration, chromolithograph, flag

items.title: A Puritan's Wife
items.description_narrative: A woman in a lace-trimmed red-and-black gown looks out serenely, one hand raised to a spray of pink roses, framed by ornate lettering and a small heraldic shield. Violet Oakley designed this book cover between 1910 and 1920.
items.tags: book cover, portrait, roses, heraldry, art nouveau, lettering

items.title: The Two Distilleries on the Same Hill
items.description_narrative: Two grotesque, ornately dressed figures raise matching glasses beneath twin drips falling from a black, twin-peaked hill topped with a dense cluster of factory buildings, the whole design rendered in stark black, white, and yellow. Harry Clarke made this illustration in 1925.
items.tags: art nouveau, grotesque figures, symmetry, factories, black and yellow, illustration
items.credit_line: Geoffrey C. Warren (1925) Elixir of Life {Uisge Beatha}. Dublin: John Jameson & Son Ltd., p. 11. [1]

items.title: Huntord's Fair Nihilist
items.description_narrative: A man in a bowler hat hurries down a staircase, glancing back over his shoulder, while another man stands above holding a framed picture near a stair rail. Wikimedia Commons attributes this illustration to Howard Pyle, reproduced in a 1913 issue of Harper's Magazine.
items.tags: magazine illustration, howard pyle, harper's magazine, golden age illustration, staircase, chase scene, suspense

items.title: Lincoln's Last Day
items.description_narrative: A man sits at a paper-strewn desk beneath crowded pigeonhole files, an apple and pen in hand, gazing off in thought as light falls across a richly patterned red rug. Howard Pyle's illustration shows Lincoln at his desk, painted in 1907.
items.tags: abraham lincoln, desk, portrait, study, oil painting, historical

items.title: Peire Vidal Chante à la Belle Azalais
items.description_narrative: A woman in a flowered wreath sings while plucking a lute, standing behind a seated woman in a patterned blue-and-gold gown who gazes downward in quiet thought. Howard Pyle painted this scene in 1903 for Harper's Magazine.
items.tags: musician, lute, medieval dress, portrait pair, illustration, harper's magazine

items.title: In the Train of King Alfonso
items.description_narrative: Two tall poplars frame a full moon as a red-robed rider on a white horse leads a torch-and-banner procession past a line of retainers carrying spears. Howard Pyle painted this nocturnal cavalcade in 1903 for Harper's Magazine.
items.tags: night procession, horseback rider, medieval costume, moonlight, illustration, pageantry

items.title: They Questioned Him with Malevolent Persistence
items.description_narrative: Two men with hands bound behind them and red sashes at their waists stand before a raised bench of black-robed judges, a tense crowd pressing close behind, one figure raising a fist. Howard Pyle painted this courtroom scene in 1910.
items.tags: courtroom, judges, prisoners, crowd, historical drama, oil painting

items.title: 'And See That You Watch Well,' He Snarled
items.description_narrative: An old man in a broad hat and weathered cloak leans on a staff, his brow furrowed as he faces a sharply dressed younger man who gestures with open hands, the two caught mid-exchange in a dim, shelf-lined room. Howard Pyle painted this magazine illustration in 1910.
items.tags: howard pyle, illustration, confrontation, interior scene, magazine art, dramatic lighting

items.title: The Apparition
items.description_narrative: A man in a green frock coat recoils, gripping a chair for support, as a pale, half-formed female figure emerges from the shadows beside him, barely more than a face and a hand holding flowers. Howard Pyle painted this ghost-story illustration in 1908.
items.tags: howard pyle, ghost story, apparition, chiaroscuro, illustration, supernatural, period costume

items.title: The Rescue at Sea
items.description_narrative: A woman in a flowing red gown reaches toward a man slumped in a small rowboat as a great galleon with pale gold sails looms behind them on a green sea. This watercolor scene dates to 1911.
items.tags: shipwreck, rescue, rowboat, galleon, watercolor, sea

items.title: The Marketplace
items.description_narrative: A young man in a green tunic and brown hose carries a bundle past baskets of fruit spilled on the cobblestones, while veiled and cloaked women gather near a vine-draped doorway of a sunbaked building. This watercolor market scene dates to 1911.
items.tags: marketplace, street scene, watercolor, medieval dress, fruit baskets, illustration

items.title: The Bride in Green
items.description_narrative: A young woman in an emerald gown embroidered in gold stands beside an ornate screen, a pale veil trailing from her head as she looks down demurely, one end of her long green train pooling at her feet. This watercolor and ink illustration is dated 1911.
items.tags: bride, fairy tale, watercolor, gown, illustration, pentamerone

items.title: The Death of Amfortas
items.description_narrative: An elderly, bearded man in white robes kneels in anguish, fist clenched to his chest, as a winged, haloed figure bends over him with wings outstretched. Edwin Austin Abbey painted this scene, titled The Death of Amfortas, in 1902.
items.tags: edwin austin abbey, angel, grail legend, mourning, allegory, illustration

items.title: The Loathly Damsel
items.description_narrative: A kneeling knight receives something from a hooded, cloaked figure beside a caparisoned white horse, while a pale woman looks on from the shadows in a scene built from deep blacks and soft grays. Edwin Austin Abbey painted this in 1902.
items.tags: knight, hooded figure, medieval, monochrome, oil painting, mystery

items.title: Baron Steuben Drilling Troops at Valley Forge
items.description_narrative: A line of ragged soldiers drills in the snow, muskets raised, as an officer in a red-lined coat and cocked hat strides down the line pointing corrections, a snowbound camp of cabins spreading behind them. Edwin Austin Abbey painted this Valley Forge scene before 1911.
items.tags: edwin austin abbey, valley forge, revolutionary war, winter drill, continental army, illustration, snow

items.title: Who Is Sylvia? What Is She, That All the Swains Commend Her?
items.description_narrative: A woman in a pale gown trimmed with gold stands at the center of a richly dressed group, a beaded pouch at her waist, as a lute player in flowing red robes performs behind her and a man in black leans against a carved stone pillar nearby. Edwin Austin Abbey painted this large canvas between 1896 and 1900.
items.tags: renaissance dress, lute player, group portrait, oil painting, ornate interior, theatrical
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: And the Fool, He Called Her His Lady Fair
items.description_narrative: A dapper older man bows low over a sofa where a skeletal woman reclines in an extravagant feathered gown, cigarette in hand and jewels at her throat, wilted flowers scattered on the floor and a wine bottle at her elbow. Charles Dana Gibson drew this pen-and-ink scene in 1917.
items.tags: charles dana gibson, satire, pen and ink, skeleton, high society, vanitas, illustration

items.title: Will Rogers Memorial Fund Poster
items.description_narrative: A weathered man in a broad hat and knotted kerchief holds coils of rope, a crowned female figure draped in stars and stripes rising behind him with a laurel branch. Howard Chandler Christy painted this poster in 1935.
items.tags: poster, lasso, personification, patriotic imagery, portrait, lettering

items.title: Roping Horses in the Corral
items.description_narrative: A cowboy in a wide-brimmed hat coils a lasso in the foreground while another rider swings a rope through dust and startled horses in a crowded corral behind him. N. C. Wyeth painted this scene in 1904.
items.tags: cowboy, lasso, corral, horses, dust, oil painting

items.title: Fourth of July
items.description_narrative: A colonial figure in a red coat and tricorne hat stands in a swordsman's stance, blade in one hand and an unfurled scroll raised in the other, beneath the Harper's Round Table masthead and a Fourth of July banner below. Maxfield Parrish drew this pen-and-ink cover in 1895.
items.tags: maxfield parrish, fourth of july, colonial, patriotic, magazine cover, pen and ink

items.title: Drifting Before the Storm
items.description_narrative: A cowboy on horseback pushes through blinding snow, driving cattle across a blizzard-swept plain as a second rider trails behind in the whiteout. Frederic Remington painted this winter range scene in 1904.
items.tags: frederic remington, cattle drive, blizzard, cowboys, winter, american west

items.title: Gathering of the Trappers
items.description_narrative: A rider on a rearing white horse charges through a field of sagebrush, whip raised, as other mounted men race behind him and a dog bolts alongside through the grass. Frederic Remington painted this scene in 1904.
items.tags: frederic remington, trappers, horses, american west, sagebrush, dog, illustration

items.title: On the White Man's Road
items.description_narrative: A rider in a plain, pale garment sits astride a bay-and-white pinto horse mid-stride across open grassland, rendered in soft monochrome tones. Frederic Remington painted this scene in 1890.
items.tags: horseback rider, pinto horse, grassland, monochrome, oil painting, plains

items.title: On the March to the Yalu
items.description_narrative: A soldier in a heavy coat and cap raises his arm in signal beside a line of laden pack animals and porters resting on a snowy mountain trail, rendered in muted grays. Frederic Remington made this scene in 1904.
items.tags: military, pack animals, snow, mountain trail, monochrome, illustration

items.title: The Flowers
items.description_narrative: Two children kneel together in a mossy garden bed, examining a flowering rosebush at close range, one in a pale shirt and the other in a rose-pink smock. Elizabeth Shippen Green drew this scene for the same 1908 Harper's Magazine story as its companion illustration.
items.tags: illustration, children, garden, flowers, golden age of illustration, harper's magazine

items.title: The Flowers
items.medium: Colour halftone reproduction of a painting, printed in Harper's Monthly Magazine, vol. 117 (1908), p. 328
items.description_narrative: An older man in overalls and spectacles bends over rows of blooming plants inside a greenhouse, marking a stem while a barefoot child looks up at him. Illustrated by Elizabeth Shippen Green, the image survives as a color halftone reproduction printed in Harper's Monthly Magazine in 1908, page 328.
items.tags: illustration, greenhouse, flowers, golden age of illustration, magazine reproduction, harper's magazine

items.title: Her Eyes Are Doves
items.description_narrative: A woman in a dark cloak and headscarf walks along a wind-battered ridge, one end of her scarf whipping loose as mist and jagged rock rise around her. Elizabeth Shippen Green drew this magazine illustration in 1910.
items.tags: elizabeth shippen green, windswept, cloak, mountain, magazine illustration, charcoal

items.title: The Little Silver Heart
items.description_narrative: A girl sits on an attic floor among open trunks and hatboxes, examining something small held in her hands while a large bare rafter slants overhead. Elizabeth Shippen Green drew this charcoal scene for a 1906 Harper's Magazine story.
items.tags: illustration, charcoal, attic, children, golden age of illustration, harper's magazine

items.title: The Little Silver Heart
items.description_narrative: A young woman in a wide-brimmed hat leans over a canopied bed, clasping the hand of an elderly figure propped against the pillows in a lace nightcap. Floral curtains and a ruffled bed skirt fill the drawing, made by Elizabeth Shippen Green for the same 1906 Harper's story.
items.tags: illustration, charcoal, bedroom, golden age of illustration, harper's magazine, figures

items.title: The Little Silver Heart
items.description_narrative: Ferns unfurl at the base of a weathered boulder where two girls in broad hats sit in quiet, close conversation, framed by bare trees. Elizabeth Shippen Green made this illustration in 1906.
items.tags: girls, conversation, rocks, ferns, outdoors, illustration

items.title: June Flowers
items.description_narrative: Layers of veiled faces crowd together beneath wreaths of white blossom, some eyes lowered, some looking straight out, a cluster of brides rendered in soft blues and creams. Rose O'Neill made this cover image in 1905.
items.tags: brides, veils, flowers, soft palette, cover illustration, women

items.title: Sure to Enjoy It
items.description_narrative: An older couple in evening dress, dripping with jewelry and feathered hats, beam down at a girl in a striped gown peeking out between them. Rose O'Neill drew this cover scene in 1901.
items.tags: evening dress, jewelry, family, cover illustration, portrait group, chromolithograph

items.title: In Georgia
items.description_narrative: Chickens scatter near a farmhouse porch as an elderly man draws a young boy close on a garden path, while a woman in a patterned dress and headscarf watches from the doorway with a baby in her arms. Rose O'Neill drew this softly colored rural scene in 1900.
items.tags: rural scene, farmyard, genre illustration, family, chickens, early 1900s

items.title: Immaterial
items.description_narrative: On a magazine cover, a woman in a checked shawl gestures mid-conversation in a cottage doorway, while a boy in a cap and an older woman holding an infant look on from a bench beside her. This is the cover of Puck, titled Immaterial, drawn by Rose O'Neill in 1901.
items.tags: rose o'neill, puck magazine, satire, cottage scene, caricature, magazine cover
